papers.title_in_file: Quantum-assisted Rendezvous on Graphs: Explicit Algorithms and Quantum Computer Simulations
papers.what_it_is: Explicit quantum protocols for one-step rendezvous games on cycle and cubic graphs, simulated and run on an IBM NISQ processor.

assertions.value: The authors report that, simulated on real NISQ hardware, they observed a near full quantum advantage for the N = 3 cycle graph problem.
quotes: When these quantum games were simulated using real NISQ hardware, we observed a near full quantum advantage for the N = 3 cycle graph problem.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical hardware result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors report sub-classical performance on real NISQ hardware for the cubic graph, which they say is consistent with the known error rates of the hardware and the much deeper quantum circuits.
quotes: In contrast, for the cubic graph, we encountered sub-classical performance, consistent with the known error rates of the hardware we used and the much deeper quantum circuits.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical hardware result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that the simulations were carried out on local classical hardware and on the 127-qubit quantum processor ibmq_brisbane.
quotes: The simulations were carried out on local classical hardware and on the 127-qubit quantum processor ibmq_brisbane [33].
assertions.certainty_reason: Paper's statement of its own experimental setup, Section 6, p.31.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum-Informed Machine Learning for Predicting Spatiotemporal Chaos with Practical Quantum Advantage
papers.what_it_is: A hybrid framework in which an offline-trained quantum generative prior guides a classical autoregressive predictor of chaotic fluid systems.

assertions.value: The authors report that QIML improves predictive distribution accuracy by up to 17.25% and full-spectrum fidelity by up to 29.36% relative to classical baselines across the systems studied.
quotes: QIML improves predictive distribution accuracy by up to 17.25% and full-spectrum fidelity by up to 29.36% relative to classical
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The title phrase practical quantum advantage is the authors' framing; the baselines are classical models.

assertions.value: The authors state that the quantum generator is trained offline and held fixed because the limited scalability and noise of NISQ superconducting devices make full end-to-end quantum training infeasible at present.
quotes: This architectural constraint arises from the limited scalability and noise of NISQ superconducting devices, which make full end-to-end quantum training infeasible at present.
assertions.certainty_reason: Paper's own stated limit, Section 3.4 p.26.

assertions.value: The authors state that the Q-Priors in this paper use as few as 10 to 15 qubits.
quotes: enabling expressive modelling with as few as 10 to 15 qubits for the systems in this paper.
assertions.certainty_reason: Paper's statement of its own setup.

papers.title_in_file: Unconditional Quantum Advantage for Sampling with Shallow Circuits
papers.what_it_is: Proves an input-independent sampling separation between constant-depth quantum circuits and bounded fan-in classical circuits with bounded random input.

assertions.value: The paper proves unconditionally that constant-depth quantum circuits can sample from distributions that constant-depth bounded fan-in classical circuits cannot reproduce, even up to additive error.
assertions.anchor: Abstract and Theorem 3, p.1 and p.4
quotes: This gives an unconditional proof that constant-depth quantum circuits can sample from distributions that
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 3 and Corollary 4, Section 1.1.

assertions.value: The authors state that the separation is shown when the number of random input bits given to the classical circuit is bounded.
quotes: we show that the answer to this question is yes when the number of random input bits given to the classical circuit is bounded.
assertions.certainty_reason: Paper's statement of the scope of its result, abstract.

assertions.value: The authors list as an open question whether the limitation on the number of inputs to the classical circuit can be removed.
quotes: Can we get rid of the limitation on the number of inputs to the classical circuit?
assertions.certainty_reason: Paper's stated limit, Section 2 Discussion and Open Problems.

papers.title_in_file: A quantum machine learning classifier to search for new physics
papers.what_it_is: Proposes quantum searching neighbor (QSN) and variational QSN classifiers and applies them to collider new-physics searches.

assertions.value: The authors state that the results indicate VQSN demonstrates superior efficiency in computational complexity to the classical k-nearest neighbor algorithm, even for classical data.
quotes: The results indicate that the VQSN demonstrates superior efficiency in the sense of computational complexity to a classical counterpart k-nearest neighbor algorithm, even when dealing with classical data.
assertions.certainty_reason: Author claim from one study.

assertions.value: The authors report that VQSN achieves the same order of magnitude of discriminative power as KNN while requiring one order of magnitude less computational cost in the three applications.
quotes: the VQSN is capable of achieving the same order of magnitude of the discriminative power to that of the KNN, while requiring one order of magnitude less cc in the three applications.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that, because the large test set would consume too much machine time, they performed the quantum computation only on a simulator for one of the analyses.
quotes: we only performed the simulation of quantum computation on a simulator
assertions.certainty_reason: Paper's own stated limit, Section 3.4 p.25.

papers.title_in_file: Supervised binary classification of small-scale digit images and weighted graphs with a trapped-ion quantum processor
papers.what_it_is: Benchmarks a trapped-ion processor with a quantum-enhanced support vector machine on tiny digit and graph datasets.

assertions.value: The authors report classifiers with 100% accuracy on both training and testing datasets in all experiments conducted.
quotes: we achieve classifiers with 100% accuracy on both training and testing datasets.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study on small datasets.

assertions.value: The authors state that the digit images were intentionally selected so that they could be classified with 100% accuracy.
quotes: For the first dataset, images are intentionally selected so that they could be classified with 100% accuracy.
assertions.certainty_reason: Paper's statement of its own dataset scope, abstract.

assertions.value: The authors report a clear exponential increase in infidelity with the number of entangling gates used, as expected.
quotes: which confirms the expectation that the performance of the circuit implementation degrades with the number of entangling gates used.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that they use a quantum-enhanced support vector machine algorithm with up to five qubits for supervised binary classification.
quotes: Using a quantum-enhanced support vector machine algorithm with up to five qubits we perform a supervised binary classification
assertions.certainty_reason: Paper's statement of its own setup, abstract.

papers.title_in_file: Predicting quantum learnability from landscape fluctuation
papers.what_it_is: Introduces a relative-fluctuation metric to predict whether a quantum neural network can learn a given target, with Clifford-sampling estimation and a lower bound.

assertions.value: The authors state that the metric shows surprising effectiveness in predicting learnability as it unifies the effects of insufficient expressibility, barren plateaus, bad local minima, and overparametrization, and report extensive numerical experiments on physical and random Hamiltonians.
quotes: This metric shows surprising effectiveness in predicting learnability as it unifies the effects of insufficient expressibility, barren plateaus, bad local minima, and overparametrization.
We conduct extensive numerical experiments to validate its effectiveness regarding physical and random Hamiltonians.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from numerical experiments in one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that the metric can be estimated efficiently on classical computers via Clifford sampling without actual training on quantum devices.
quotes: it can be estimated efficiently on classical computers via Clifford sampling without actual training on quantum devices.
assertions.certainty_reason: Author claim in the abstract.

assertions.value: The authors prove a lower bound on the landscape fluctuation for a PQC composed of blocks forming independent local 2-designs and an r-local Hamiltonian.
quotes: We also prove a compact lower bound for the metric in locally scrambled circuits as analytical guidance.
Theorem 1 For a PQC composed of blocks forming independent local 2-designs and an rlocal Hamiltonian, the landscape fluctuation is lower bounded by
assertions.certainty_reason: Theorem 1, p.3 (proof in the appendix).

assertions.value: The authors state that they mainly focus on physical scenarios where the learning target is encoded in Hamiltonians.
quotes: In addition, here we mainly focus on physical scenarios where the learning target is encoded in Hamiltonians.
assertions.certainty_reason: Paper's own stated scope, Section 5 p.6.

papers.title_in_file: QuanGCN: Noise-Adaptive Training for Robust Quantum Graph Convolutional Networks
papers.what_it_is: Proposes a quantum graph convolutional network with sparse-pooling and skip-connection noise mitigation, tested on a simulator and IBMQ-Quito.

assertions.value: The authors state that their experimental results show QuanGCN is functionally comparable or even superior to the classical algorithms on several benchmark graph datasets.
quotes: The experimental results show that our QuanGCN is functionally comparable or even superior than the classical algorithms on several benchmark graph datasets.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that the numbers of qubits and graph convolutional layers are set to 4 and 2, respectively.
quotes: The numbers of qubits and graph convolutional layers are set to 4 and 2, respectively.
assertions.certainty_reason: Paper's statement of its own setup, Section 3 p.5.

assertions.value: The authors state that they test the QNNs only once on the real device because of queuing time.
quotes: Since the inference in real quantum computer has to pay plenty of queuing time, we test QNNs only once in the real device.
assertions.certainty_reason: Paper's own stated limit, Section 3 p.5.

assertions.value: The authors report that QNNs generally have lower accuracies on the quantum device than in GPU inference, which they attribute to high error rates.
quotes: Comparing with the inference performances in GPUs (i.e., in Table 1), QNNs generally have lower accuracies due to the high error rates existing inherently in the quantum devices.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study, single run on hardware.

papers.title_in_file: On quantum ensembles of quantum classifiers
papers.what_it_is: Shows that the accuracy-weighted quantum ensemble can be dequantised and that the general quantum ensemble framework contains the Deutsch-Jozsa algorithm.

assertions.value: The authors state that the accuracy-weighted quantum ensemble, a specific implementation of the quantum ensemble of quantum classifiers, can be fully dequantised.
quotes: we demonstrate that a specific implementation of the quantum ensemble of quantum classifiers, called the accuracy-weighted quantum ensemble, can be fully dequantised.
assertions.certainty_reason: Shown analytically in the dequantisation section; abstract and Conclusion p.5.

assertions.value: The authors state that the general quantum ensemble framework is shown to contain the Deutsch-Jozsa algorithm, which provides a quantum speedup.
quotes: the general quantum ensemble framework is shown to contain the well-known Deutsch-Jozsa algorithm that notably provides a quantum speedup
assertions.certainty_reason: Shown in the section linking Deutsch-Jozsa and the quantum ensemble framework.

assertions.value: The authors state that the Deutsch-Jozsa reduction does not necessarily represent a quantum ensemble that is useful for machine learning.
quotes: does not necessarily represent a quantum ensemble that is useful for machine learning.
assertions.certainty_reason: Paper's own stated limit, Conclusion p.5.
